api_access: FREE. ||| AUTH (CONFIRMED): a Subscription-Key issued free from https://api.edinet-fsa.go.jp/api/auth/index.aspx?mode=1, passed as a QUERY-STRING parameter `Subscription-Key=` (not a header). Keys are self-service re-issuable; password reset and MFA clearing are documented in spec §2-3-2. ||| ENDPOINTS (CONFIRMED, spec §3-1 and §3-2): (1) 書類一覧API (document list) GET https://api.edinet-fsa.go.jp/api/v2/documents.json?date=YYYY-MM-DD&type={1|2}&Subscription-Key=KEY — type=1 metadata only, type=2 metadata + full submitted-document list (type omitted defaults to 1). `date` is MANDATORY and accepts exactly ONE calendar date per call; there is no from/to range, no company filter, no docType filter and no pagination. (2) 書類取得API (document retrieval) GET https://api.edinet-fsa.go.jp/api/v2/documents/{docID}?type={1..5}&Subscription-Key=KEY where type=1 提出本文書及び監査報告書 (ZIP: PublicDoc/AuditDoc folders + inline-XBRL or XBRL instance + manifest + taxonomy; note XbrlSearchDlInfo.csv is NOT included because its content is already in the list API), type=2 PDF, type=3 代替書面・添付文書 (ZIP; PDFs embedded in attachments are ONLY obtainable here, not via type=2), type=4 英文ファイル (ZIP), type=5 CSV (ZIP; the document's XBRL converted to CSV). Availability of each rendition is signalled per-document by the list API flags xbrlFlag/pdfFlag/attachDocFlag/englishDocFlag/csvFlag. ||| PROTOCOL (CONFIRMED): GET only; TLS 1.2 or above; cross-domain (CORS) requests are explicitly NOT permitted, so browser-side JavaScript cannot call the API — server-side only. For the retrieval API you must branch on the response Content-Type header to detect failure, because a failed call still returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body where a ZIP was expected. 401 uses a different body shape ({'StatusCode':401,'message':...}) than 400/404/500 ({'metadata':{'title','status','message'}}). ||| RATE LIMITS (PARTIALLY CONFIRMED — no number is published): HTTP-status 429 'Too Many Requests' exists and was newly documented in spec revision 2.8 (2026-05); its remedy text is '一定時間内に大量のリクエストを受信しました。十分な時間を空けて再試行してください。また、取得間隔を見直してください。' — i.e. throttling is real but the FSA deliberately publishes NO requests/second, /minute or /day figure. FAQ (API Q14) states 'EDINET APIに限らず、処理能力に支障が生じた際にアクセス制限を行う場合があります' (access restriction may be imposed when capacity is impaired). INFERRED: for backfill work, self-throttle to roughly 1 request/second or slower with exponential backoff on 429; do not assume any guaranteed throughput. ||| ENGLISH DOCUMENTS (CONFIRMED but weak): englishDocFlag + type=4 return an English file only where the filer voluntarily submitted one; the spec notes type=1 excludes '外国会社の英文報告本文'. update_frequency: CONFIRMED (spec §3-1-3): CURRENT DAY — data is refreshed from about 08:30 JST, in principle once every minute; the current-day file is replaced even when nothing changed, so processDateTime always moves. Recommended polling per FAQ is therefore once per minute or slower. PAST DAYS — a nightly job (日次更新処理) starting just after 24:00 JST rewrites EVERY past file date (not just changed ones), applies legalStatus transitions, applies withdrawal and finance-bureau-correction/non-disclosure status changes, and DELETES file dates that have passed 10 years. The nightly job creates the new current-day file LAST, so the appearance of today's file is the reliable signal that the previous day's data is final. CONFIRMED caveat: because the list is refreshed on a schedule, a document can appear in the list as 'in disclosure' while already being unavailable from the retrieval API — retrieval failures on freshly listed rows are expected and must be retried later. Also CONFIRMED: magnetic-disk and paper filings are listed under the OPERATION date, not the filing date, so a document with a past submission date can appear in today's list (opeDateTime is set in that case) — a backfill that only ever reads each date once will therefore miss late-registered filings unless you re-read recent dates.
limitations: 1. FATAL FOR THE STATED GOAL — a 10-year M&A deal history CANNOT be built from EDINET alone. CONFIRMED: 臨時報告書 (the primary M&A event report), 公開買付届出書 and 大量保有報告書/変更報告書 all have 5-year viewing periods with NO extension, and the list-API date parameter is capped at a rolling 10 years anyway. Years 6-10 of M&A events are simply gone and cannot be recovered from EDINET at any price. Only 有価証券報告書/半期報告書/四半期報告書 reach back 10 years. 2. CONFIRMED call arithmetic: one call per calendar date, so 5 years = 1,827 calls and the full 10-year window = 3,653 calls, using documents.json?date=YYYY-MM-DD&type=2. Use type=2 (not type=1) so you get the rows, not just a count. At a self-imposed 1 request/second the full 10-year backfill is ~1 hour of wall clock and roughly 300-600MB of JSON; at the conservative 1 request/minute implied by the FAQ it is ~61 hours, so run it as a resumable job with a per-date checkpoint table. Retry 429 with exponential backoff, and remember the status is inside the JSON body, not the HTTP status. Filter the list rows to docTypeCode in (180,190) and parse currentReportReason for the M&A article citations enumerated under ma_relevance — this alone yields a dated, classified, acquirer-identified M&A event stream at zero document-download cost. Because the statutory item labels are fixed by 開示府令 (商号 / 本店の所在地 / 代表者の氏名 / 資本金又は出資の額 / 純資産の額 / 総資産の額 / 事業の内容 / 売上高 / 営業利益 / 経常利益 / 純利益 / 子会社取得の目的 / 子会社取得の対価の額), a label-anchored extractor over the iXBRL text blocks and tables is the right first design — validate on ~30 real 第8号の2 documents before committing. LISTED COMPANIES ONLY. TDnet has nothing on unlisted acquirers or unlisted targets, so the largest gap in Japanese mid-market M&A coverage is untouched. Where a listed company buys an unlisted target, the target appears only as text in a PDF, exactly as in EDINET. 5. TDnetDBS has no API and no bulk export — human research only. 10. TDnetDBS excludes AGM convocation notices. 11. Contracting is manual and multi-step (application, fee confirmation, fee agreement, key issuance) with no published lead time. 12. INFERRED: no numeric materiality thresholds for the M&A disclosure items were located in any fetched JPX source — see ma_relevance for what can and cannot be concluded.
ma_relevance: HIGH for event DETECTION and COMPLETENESS; low for structured deal terms. This is the best available paid complement to EDINET, and the reason is a genuine regime difference rather than a data-processing difference. ||| WHY IT ADDS TO EDINET: EDINET's 臨時報告書 obligations are gated by hard statutory materiality tests (子会社取得 consideration ≥15% of net assets; 吸収合併/吸収分割 ≥10% of net assets or ≥3% of sales; 事業譲渡・譲受 ≥30% of net assets or ≥10% of sales; consolidated-subsidiary equivalents ≥30% of consolidated net assets). TDnet's disclosure-item taxonomy, by contrast, contains a code — 117 子会社等の異動を伴う株式又は持分の譲渡又は取得その他の子会社等の異動を伴う事項 — whose SCOPE IS DEFINED BY THE EVENT (any share or equity transfer/acquisition that changes subsidiary status), not by a consideration-to-net-assets ratio, and separate codes for 合併, 会社分割, 事業譲渡・譲受, 株式交換, 株式移転, 株式交付 and 固定資産の譲渡・取得 at issuer, subsidiary AND parent level. INFERRED (well-reasoned but NOT directly confirmed): TDnet therefore surfaces a materially larger population of M&A events than EDINET — in particular the sub-15%-of-net-assets bolt-on acquisitions by large-cap acquirers that generate no 臨時報告書 at all — because exchange timely-disclosure rules operate on their own 軽微基準 (de-minimis standards) under the listing rules rather than on the FIEA thresholds. IMPORTANT HONESTY FLAG: no fetched JPX source states the numeric 軽微基準, and I did not obtain the TSE listing rules text in this research. The DIRECTION of the difference is well supported by the code definitions being event-scoped; the MAGNITUDE is unverified and must be measured empirically (see implementation_notes). ||| WHAT THE INDEX GIVES YOU DIRECTLY: 銘柄コード (which joins cleanly to the EDINET code list's 証券コード column and thence to 法人番号), 銘柄略称, 開示日付, 開示時刻 to the minute, 表題 (the disclosure title, which in Japanese practice almost always names the counterparty and the transaction structure — e.g. '株式取得（子会社化）に関するお知らせ'), 開示番号 for document retrieval, 取扱属性 to catch revisions and deletions, and one or more 公開項目コード. That is a complete, dated, classified, acquirer-identified M&A event stream for every Japanese listed company — and on the TDnet API it costs NOTHING beyond the JPY 70,000/month base fee, because index retrieval is explicitly not metered. ||| WHAT IT DOES NOT GIVE: the counterparty's identity as a resolved entity, the consideration, the target's financials, or any structured deal field — all of that is inside the full-text PDF. Note the asymmetry with EDINET here: EDINET's 臨時報告書 第8号の2 legally COMPELS disclosure of the target's name, head office, representative, capital, net assets, total assets, business description, three years of P&L, and the consideration amount. TDnet compels no such schedule. So EDINET gives fewer deals with far richer mandated content; TDnet gives more deals with thinner mandated content. They are complements, not substitutes, and neither alone is sufficient. ||| Adjacent M&A signals available only here: 116 業務上の提携 (alliances, which frequently precede acquisitions), 121 上場廃止申請 (the completion signal for a take-private), 405 公開買付け等事実の公表, and the English-release codes as a cross-border proxy.
implementation_notes: RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE — do the free work first, and do not buy anything until step 2 has produced a number. ||| STEP 1 (free, ~1 day): integrate against the public test server at https://apidoc-tdnet.jpx-dataservice.com using the published access key. api_access: BOTH FREE. ||| gBizINFO (CONFIRMED, read from the OpenAPI 3 spec at https://api.info.gbiz.go.jp/hojin/v3/api-docs — 94KB, located in this research after the Swagger UI proved to be an unfetchable JavaScript shell): auth is an API token in the HTTP header `X-hojinInfo-api-token`. Endpoints exist in both v1 and v2 families: /v{1,2}/hojin (search), /v{1,2}/hojin/{corporate_number} (detail), and per-aspect sub-resources /certification, /commendation, /finance, /patent, /procurement, /subsidy, /workplace, plus /v2/hojin/{corporate_number}/corporation; a parallel /v{1,2}/hojin/updateInfo family returns recently changed records for each aspect; and standalone suggest endpoints /SuggestNames, /SuggestBusinessNames, /SuggestNcrNames, /SuggestSubsidyNames, /SuggestTrademarks. Response fields on the corporation object include corporate_number, name, name_en, location, postal_code, business_items, capital_stock, employee_number, date_of_establishment, company_url, representative_name, close_cause, qualification_grade and update_date. The /v2/hojin SEARCH accepts a genuinely screening-capable parameter set: name, prefecture, city, corporate_type, capital_stock_from/to, employee_number_from/to, founded_year, net_sales_summary_of_business_results_from/to, total_assets_summary_of_business_results_from/to, procurement_amount_from/to, subsidy_amount_from/to, certification, patent, procurement, subsidy, ministry, exist_flg, average_age, average_continuous_service_years, female_workers_proportion, month_average_predetermined_overtime_hours, source, metadata_flg, from, to, page, limit. Getting the API key requires a web application at https://info.gbiz.go.jp/hojin/various_registration/form supplying the applicant's own 法人番号, corporate name, department, e-mail, password and declared purpose of use, plus acceptance of the API・データダウンロード利用規約; a confirmation e-mail then carries a URL from which the token is retrieved. NOT CONFIRMED: rate limits (no requests/second, /day or /month figure appears on any fetched page), and the approval turnaround. ||| NTA (CONFIRMED, read from the official spec PDF): auth is an アプリケーションID passed as `id=` in the query string. Three endpoint families, with version = 1-4 (name search supports 2-4 only): GET https://api.houjin-bangou.nta.go.jp/{version}/num?id=&number={up to 10 comma-separated corporate numbers}&type=&history={0|1}; GET .../{version}/diff?id=&from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD&type=&address=&kind=&divide=; GET .../{version}/name?id=&name={URL-encoded}&type=&mode={1|2}&target={1|2|3}&address=&kind=&change=&close=&from=&to=&divide=. Formats: type=01 CSV/Shift-JIS (JIS levels 1-2), type=02 CSV/Unicode (levels 1-4), type=12 XML/Unicode (levels 1-4). Hard per-request limits: at most 10 corporate numbers per lookup; at most a 50-DAY date range on the differential function; and any result exceeding 2,000 RECORDS paginates via divide/分割番号 and 分割数. NOT CONFIRMED: any calls-per-second or per-day quota (the spec references a separate 利用手続について（共通編） volume that was not retrieved and may contain one).
archive_window: gBizINFO: CONFIRMED it is a CURRENT-STATE registry, not a time series — it returns the present state of each company plus an update_date, with updateInfo endpoints for recently changed records. There is no historical snapshot API, so point-in-time reconstruction is impossible unless you snapshot it yourself. NOT CONFIRMED: how far back the subsidy, procurement and patent event records reach. ||| NTA: CONFIRMED it carries CHANGE HISTORY, which is unusual and valuable — the schema includes process (処理区分: new / renamed / relocated / closed etc.), correct (訂正区分), updateDate, changeDate, changeCause (変更事由の詳細), assignmentDate (法人番号指定年月日), latest (1 = current record, 0 = a past record), closeDate and closeCause (登記記録の閉鎖等年月日/事由), and successorCorporateNumber (承継先法人番号 — the surviving entity's corporate number). Corporate numbers have been issued since October 2015, so the history runs from then. History retrieval is controlled by history=1 on the number lookup. ||| WHY THIS MATTERS FOR M&A, and it is easy to miss: closeDate + closeCause + successorCorporateNumber is effectively a free, complete, authoritative national MERGER TRAIL. When a Japanese company is absorbed by merger, its registration closes and the register records the successor's corporate number. That is a machine-readable 'entity A was absorbed into entity B on date D' record covering ALL Japanese corporations — listed and unlisted, of any size, with no materiality threshold whatsoever, from 2015 onward. It carries no price and no deal narrative, so it is not a deal database; but as a way to detect that a merger happened at all among unlisted companies, nothing else identified in this research comes close, and it is free. This deserves explicit evaluation in the implementation plan.

CONFIRMED NEGATIVE: there are NO financial fields anywhere in this schema, no capital, no employee count, no industry code, no representative name, and no securities code or EDINET code. It is an identity register and nothing more.
formats: gBizINFO: CONFIRMED JSON over REST (OpenAPI 3 documented), plus website downloads in CSV, PDF and JSON. NTA: CONFIRMED CSV in Shift-JIS or Unicode and XML in Unicode, for both the API and the bulk files.
update_frequency: gBizINFO: NOT CONFIRMED — no update-frequency statement appears on any fetched page, which is itself a notable gap given that the NTA documents its cadence precisely. limitations: 1. NEITHER SERVICE CONTAINS ANY M&A DEAL INFORMATION. No transactions, no prices, no acquirer-target relationships (except the NTA merger trail described in archive_window, which carries no price and no narrative). These are infrastructure, not deal sources. 2. gBizINFO's field fill rate is UNVERIFIED and is believed to be poor for unlisted and small companies — the very population that makes it interesting. Its rich search parameters (capital, employees, sales, total assets) are only as useful as the underlying data is populated, and that was not measured here. This is the key unknown. 3. gBizINFO publishes no rate limits and no update frequency, so its operational characteristics cannot be planned. 4. gBizINFO's Swagger UI is a JavaScript shell that returns no usable text to fetch tools; the machine-readable spec at /hojin/v3/api-docs was found only by probing, and adjacent guessed paths return 404 or 500 — the documentation surface is fragile. 5. gBizINFO's API terms confine usage to the purpose declared at application time, and redistribution is not explicitly addressed for the API/download terms specifically (the main site terms permit broad reuse including commercial with attribution). Minor residual ambiguity; low risk. 6. NTA has no financials, no industry classification, no representative name, no capital and no employee count — it cannot support target screening on its own. 7. NTA's per-request limits are restrictive for bulk work: 10 corporate numbers per lookup, a 50-day maximum date range on differentials, and 2,000-record pagination. Use the bulk files instead of the API for any large-scale matching. 8. NTA's application turnaround is 2 weeks to 1 month, so it is a lead-time item; the bulk downloads need no application and can be used immediately. 9. NEITHER SERVICE PROVIDES AN EDINET-CODE OR SECURITIES-CODE CROSSWALK. CONFIRMED for NTA (the 36-field schema is exhaustive and contains neither); INFERRED for gBizINFO (nothing in the fetched spec or pages shows such a field). 10. NTA requires a specific disclaimer to be displayed on derived content (see below), and prohibits transferring, lending or disclosing the Application ID to third parties. 11. Neither service supports point-in-time reconstruction of gBizINFO attributes; only NTA carries history, and only from 2015. 12. gBizINFO's own primary key is 法人番号, so it cannot be entered from a company NAME as effectively as NTA can.
ma_relevance: LOW as a deal source; HIGH as the entity-resolution and screening substrate that makes an EDINET pipeline usable. ||| THE PROBLEM THESE SOLVE: EDINET's M&A gold is 臨時報告書 第19条第2項第8号の2, which legally compels disclosure of the target's 商号, 本店の所在地, 代表者の氏名, capital, net assets, total assets, business description and three years of P&L — but the target is almost never an EDINET filer, so it arrives as FREE TEXT with no identifier of any kind. Without resolution, every acquired target is an orphan string and the deal history cannot be joined to the firm's Salesforce Account universe or to any screening work. ||| THE RESOLUTION PIPELINE (recommended, based on confirmed capabilities): (1) Resolve the target's free-text name to a 法人番号 using the NTA name-search function, which is purpose-built for exactly this — CONFIRMED to support forward-match, partial-match and fuzzy modes with kana normalisation (mode, target parameters), plus English-name and furigana fields, and to cover the entire national corporate register with twice-daily updates. The 本店の所在地 that the ordinance compels the filer to disclose is a powerful disambiguator here: combine name plus prefecture/city (the address parameter) to cut through Japan's very high rate of duplicate company names. Prefer the free bulk full-file plus daily deltas over per-name API calls, given the 10-number and 2,000-record request limits. (2) Enrich from gBizINFO using 法人番号 as the join key, adding capital, employee count, establishment date, representative, industry items, URL, and any subsidy/procurement/patent footprint — subject to the sparsity caveat. (3) Bridge to the listed universe using the EDINET コードリスト, which — as established in the EDINET record of this file — DOES contain EDINET code, 証券コード and 提出者法人番号 in one free CSV (3,820 securities codes and 7,249 corporate numbers across 11,392 rows). This is the crosswalk neither gBizINFO nor the NTA provides, and it closes the loop: target name -> 法人番号 -> (if listed) EDINET code and securities code -> TDnet 銘柄コード and J-Quants 銘柄コード. Build this spine before anything else. ||| SECONDARY M&A USES: the NTA closeDate / closeCause / successorCorporateNumber merger trail (see archive_window) as a free, threshold-free national detector of completed mergers including unlisted-to-unlisted — the single most interesting M&A-relevant finding in this record. gBizINFO's /v2/hojin search as a free first-pass origination screen for unlisted acquisition candidates by prefecture, capital, employee count, sales and total assets — genuinely aligned with a Japanese intermediary's sell-side origination work, and worth a sparsity test precisely because if the data holds up it is free lead generation. gBizINFO's updateInfo endpoints to detect corporate change events. And NTA change history to track renames and relocations so that historical deal records stay joined to entities that have since changed identity.
implementation_notes: STEP 1 (do this first, it is free and unblocks everything): download the NTA 全件データ full national file plus the daily 差分 files from https://www.houjin-bangou.nta.go.jp/download/ — no application needed, no rate limit, CSV/Unicode. Load it locally and build a name-matching index with kana and English-name normalisation. A local corpus makes resolution instant and sidesteps the API's 10-number and 2,000-record limits entirely. In parallel, apply for the NTA アプリケーションID (invoice-web-api@nta.go.jp) because approval takes 2 weeks to 1 month and you will want the name-search and diff functions for incremental work; and apply for the gBizINFO token at https://info.gbiz.go.jp/hojin/various_registration/form, declaring the purpose accurately since usage is confined to what you declare. ||| STEP 2 (the measurement that decides gBizINFO's value, half a day once the token arrives): sample a few hundred known unlisted Japanese mid-market companies and measure the actual FILL RATE of capital_stock, employee_number, date_of_establishment, representative_name, business_items and the 財務情報 fields. gBizINFO's search parameters promise a screening tool; only this test shows whether the data behind them exists. Also establish empirically whether 財務情報 is EDINET-derived (in which case it is redundant for listed companies and absent for unlisted ones) or independently sourced. Do not design any screening feature before this number is known. ||| STEP 3 (build the entity spine): a resolution service taking (name, address fragment) and returning a ranked 法人番号 candidate list with confidence scores, backed by the local NTA corpus. Expect to need a human-confirmation queue — Japanese company-name matching is genuinely hard, with duplicate 商号 across prefectures, 株式会社 prefix/suffix variation, old and new kanji forms, and the abbreviations that appear in disclosure documents. Do NOT model this as fully automatic. Then load the EDINET コードリスト as the listed-universe bridge (EDINET code <-> 証券コード <-> 法人番号) and refresh it monthly with versioning, since EDINET codes get consolidated. Effort: roughly 1-2 weeks for a decent first-pass matcher plus review UI. ||| STEP 4 (evaluate the merger trail — the highest-upside item here): prototype a scan of the NTA data for records where closeCause indicates a merger and successorCorporateNumber is populated, and assess volume, quality and usefulness. If it works, the firm gets a free, complete, threshold-free feed of completed Japanese mergers including the unlisted-to-unlisted segment that neither EDINET nor TDnet can see — precisely the coverage gap that matters most to a mid-market intermediary. Timebox it to a few days; the payoff justifies the look even if the hit rate disappoints. ||| STEP 5 (incremental operation): NTA 差分 daily; gBizINFO updateInfo endpoints on a cadence to be determined once its update frequency is known (ask METI, since it is undocumented). ||| COMPLIANCE: NTA REQUIRES this exact disclaimer on derived content — 「このサービスは、国税庁法人番号システムWeb-API機能を利用して取得した情報をもとに作成しているが、サービスの内容は国税庁によって保証されたものではない」. Never transfer, lend or disclose the Application ID. gBizINFO requires source attribution and, where content has been edited or processed, an explicit statement that modifications were made; both permit commercial use, and both disclaim accuracy and completeness. Governing law for the NTA terms is Japan with exclusive jurisdiction in the Tokyo District Court.

The merger-trail capability follows directly from the confirmed closeDate / closeCause / successorCorporateNumber fields, though its practical yield is untested. ||| MEDIUM for gBizINFO: the endpoint inventory, the X-hojinInfo-api-token header auth, the response field names and the full /v2/hojin search parameter list are CONFIRMED, having been read from the OpenAPI 3 spec at https://api.info.gbiz.go.jp/hojin/v3/api-docs, which was located by probing after the Swagger UI proved to be an unfetchable JavaScript shell (note: earlier research passes reported these as unobtainable — they are obtainable at that URL). The 5-million-plus corporation claim and the data-category list are CONFIRMED from the site.
